neighbours.label: ' some' / ' any' / ' quite' as an indefinite measure of time or distance ('for some time', 'for any length of time', 'quite a while', 'some distance'); the - pole takes the definite side (a counted duration)
fire: The shop has been empty for some time, and the windows are dusty.
Nobody who has farmed here for any length of time trusts the spring weather.
It will be some months before the road is repaired.
We had been waiting for quite a while when the bus finally came.
The old engine overheats if it is run for any distance.
She has lived abroad for quite some time now.
It may be some weeks before the results are announced.
The cabin stands some distance from the nearest road.
quiet: The shop has been empty for two years, and the windows are dusty.
Nobody who has farmed here for thirty years trusts the spring weather.
It will be six months before the road is repaired.
We had been waiting for forty minutes when the bus finally came.
Some farmers trust the spring weather more than others.
She added some salt to the soup and tasted it.
The cabin stands two miles from the nearest road.
Do you have any questions about the results?

notes: Probes: 'for some time' 0.48, 'any length of time' 0.79, 'some years before' 0.60, 'quite a while' 0.61, 'some distance' 0.38; 'for three weeks' 0.01, 'Some people' 0.03, 'some sugar' 0.17. Output promotes ' distance', ' depth', ' some', ' slightly'.
